primitives.name: Honor Integrity Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: With no disrespect to any class or condition —with the best regard for all strong legislation in outside athletic bodies —I say that the collegian's standard of purity in his sports should be the highest.
primitives.assumptions: Honor and integrity are scalar measures of moral compliance in athletic contexts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H < 0 or I < 0, constraint violation occurs.

primitives.name: Captaincy Eligibility Verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: If you are elected the captain of a nine, team, or crew, read over your rules, and note exactly who are allowed as contestants by those rules, not by the custom of some predecessor, not by what you think some rival will do, but by the rules themselves.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'set of permissible contestants under rule set', 'C': 'set of actual contestants', 'E': 'eligibility indicator function'}
primitives.assumptions: Eligibility is determined by strict adherence to formal rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E(C \ R) > 0, eligibility breach occurs.

layer2.mapping: GSE state transition from rule-read to contestant-verification.

These form a constraint manifold where each athlete must satisfy both H ≥ 0 and I ≥ 0. The captaincy verification (captaincy_eligibility_verification) acts as a projection operator onto this manifold. Failure modes arise when either moral duty is neglected or eligibility rules are violated. The system exhibits a duality between internal ethical calibration and external rule enforcement. In GSI, these map to Bayesian priors on integrity and eligibility. In GSE, they define state transitions from candidate selection to team formation. The epistemic closure is achieved through recursive verification of each actor's compliance against the defined manifolds.
